newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore port to build car storage centre.
newsitem.headline: Singapore port to build car storage centre.

text.p: The Port of Singapore Authority (PSA) is planning to build a large car storage facility at Sembawang Wharves on the island's north coast, Singapore's Communications Minister Mah Bow Tan said on Friday.
Mah said in a speech the multi-level facility would help make Singapore a specialist car transshipment centre for Asia.
Manjit Singh, PSA assistant director, told reporters the PSA would spend S$15 million (US$10.7 million) to S$20 million in 1997 on the first phase of the 14-level facility.
He said the facility would result in an initial capacity addition of 2,500 cars to the wharves' existing 5,000 to 6,000 capacity. The facility could be expanded to 5,000 in further stages, he said.
Work on the first stage was expected to begin in the second half of 1997 and would take up to 18 months.
Singh said the PSA was still reviewing automation systems and that construction tenders had not yet been invited.
Mah also said logistics -- management, storage and distribution of goods -- was now a substantial contributor to the Singapore economy, and was growing by 10 percent annually.
He said logistics was worth S$9 billion in value-added services and another S$18.9 billion in business spending to Singapore in 1995.
In addition to the Sembawang project, Singapore was redeveloping wharves at Pasir Panjang in the south and had developed an aviation distribution zone at Changi, in the east, Mah said.
